method: Before reading the unit we reread the u04 exemplar and its five review rounds (a1.1-u04.r1–r5), u03 r1 and u01 r2, and SCHEMA §15.6. We then checked every u04/u01 finding class against this unit (notes). The review read the files as they stood on disk: u03.json (last written 2026-09-27 23:14 UTC), a1.1/lexicon.json (23:03) and a1.1/rule-cards.json (23:06). Both reviewers read every German string of the current file. That covers title and title.canDo, spec.situation, spec.deviation and the lexicon block titles; the Folge (10 lines) and its gist item; the three inputs (30 lines) and Emre's chat post; both exam texts, the strategy card and the 8 redemittel. For Sp2 it covers situationDe, instructionsDe, openingLine, aiRole.personaDe, the cards, 8 hintWords and 10 model turns. For S2 it covers situationDe, taskDe, the 3 Leitpunkte and their cues, the checklist and the model text. It also covers the 3 check lines, the story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de, the 33 u03 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json, and the two rule cards the unit shows. We solved all 88 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line only: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 12 reserve items, 5 exam items, 8 check items and 2 proof items. Every key is right. For sentence building we permuted the tiles and checked each V2, V1 and declarative order against accepted[] and the prompt's frame. For error correction we tried every one-word correction and the uncorrected sentence. We ran 60 candidate learner answers through the player's own grader (src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js → src/lib/lesson/check.js) and read how ItemView.jsx resolves a TYPO (l. 70 prefills an error correction with its wrong sentence; l. 108/140–150 give one retry, then count a TYPO as correct with errorTag null). Because two answers came back TYPO where they should have been WRONG, we scanned every registered course with the same grader. The first scan tried each of the 128 error-correction items with its own quoted wrong sentence. The second tried every typed verb-form gap with its key's unchanged-vowel form (F01). The exam block was checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: l1 has 5 × richtig_falsch, 2 options and two texts of 56–92 words; sp2 has cards-ask, 2 rounds and 0 minutes' preparation; s2 has 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words, and Anrede/Gruß are not Leitpunkte. It was also checked against the rubrics sd1-sp2 and sd1-s2 and the grader: grade.mjs buildSpeakingUserPrompt passes situationDe (l. 288), and speaking-session.mjs l. 132–133 speaks the authored openingLine verbatim. We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (compile.mjs --out/--banks-out: 12 units compiled) and read the bank entry a11-u03-s. Word counts were recomputed with the validator's wordCount: t1 69, t2 73, chat 50, S2 model 29, Sp2 situation 45, cliffhanger 20. The grammar ceiling was read against grammar-spine.json and curriculum/a1-1.md §6 U3. Load was read against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 new, ±10 %; productive share 0.5 ± 0.05; subordinateClausesMax 0), and u03 has 33 entries, 15 of them productive. Can-dos were read against registries/cando/a1.json. The cast was read against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ages, origins, languages, residence, du/Sie relations). The story was read against u01, u02, u04, u05 and u08. No 360 px walkthrough was run (the walkthrough reviewer's remit).

verdict: Not exit-ready, but the unit's own content is two small edits from done. The authors landed every unit-side fix of r1: 13 of 16 findings are fixed or fixed in the unit. The validator is green (0 blockers). All 88 keys are right. The German is correct and idiomatic on every model surface. All five can-dos are performed: age, job and Herkunftsland are now asked for in Sp2. The Befinden formula is now formal where Sie is spoken. Sp2's warm-up is declared to the grader, and the story (Elif, the Oma in İzmir) agrees with the cast bible and u08. Three MAJORs stop exit, and all three are held outside u03.json. (1) New in this round: the grader forgives the unit's second new grammar point as a spelling slip. „Es schlaft schon.“, „sie lest“ and „du sprechst“ come back TYPO, and after one retry ItemView counts a TYPO as correct with no error tag. That covers all seven typed Vokalwechsel items, one of them in the scored Check. In the error correction ls2-p10, whose input is prefilled with „Er sprecht gut Deutsch.“, pressing „Prüfen“ twice passes without changing a letter. The same grader behaviour hits 9 units in 5 of the 8 courses, 5 of them in A1.1, so it is a stop-the-line class for the checker owner and the rule-smith (F01). (2) The unit's own word cards still contradict the cast: Sophie „lebt mit ihrem Partner in Dresden“. They also still show the ihr-possessive the unit must not yet teach (F02, lexicon owner, unchanged since r1). (3) lesen and schlafen, which carry the unit's productive Vokalwechsel drill, are still receptive. The new LEX-03 rail reports this only as an advisory (F03, lexicon owner, a 2-line edit). Six minors remain. Two are unit edits introduced by r1 fixes: ls3-p11's stem now ignores the named Elif (F04), and Nora's openingLine asks „Wie geht es Ihnen?“ and launches Teil 2 in the same breath (F06). One is a checker edge: a case slip on „tochter“ in ls3-p10 is WRONG and tagged register (F05). findings.problem: g.vokalwechsel is one of the unit's two new spine points, and its only error is a single vowel: „schlaft/schläft“, „lest/liest“, „sprechst/sprichst“. check.js forgives exactly that. It allows one Levenshtein-1 slip on a word of five letters or more, as long as the last letter stays, and it makes an item strict only when its topic matches STRICT_TOPIC, which was written for the live course's topic names. So all seven typed Vokalwechsel items grade the target error as a TYPO, including c03 in the scored Check. The learner reads „Fast richtig – prüfen Sie die Schreibung“, and the item is counted correct if the same form is submitted again. errorTag is null, so the miss never reaches the repair pools. The possessive items are safe only because their error changes the last letter. ls2-p10 is worse. ItemView prefills an error correction with its quoted wrong sentence, and that sentence is Levenshtein 1 from the key, so pressing „Prüfen“ twice without typing anything passes the item. The r1-F03 gap adds to it: ErrorTag has no verb-form value, so even a WRONG Vokalwechsel answer feeds no repair pool (ITM-12). No rule runs the grader on an item's wrong forms (ITM-13 does so for dictations only), so every gate passed. The class is course-wide. Among the 128 error corrections in all registered courses, the uncorrected sentence grades TYPO in a1.1-u03-ls2-p10, a1.1-u10-ls2-p10 („Du fahrst am Abend zurück.“), a1.2-u04-ls3-p11 („Ich hatte gern …“), a2.2-u04-ls2-p10 („Du wirdst …“) and b1.2-u04-ls3-p10 („…, das wir …“). The unchanged-vowel form of a typed verb gap grades TYPO in a1.1-u03 (7 items), a1.1-u07 („fangt“ ×4), a1.1-u08 („trefft“), a1.1-u10 („fahrt“, „fahrst“, „trefft“), a1.1-u12 („fangt“), a1.2-u04 („hatte“ for Konjunktiv „hätte“) and b2.1-u04 („hatte/hatten“). Five A1.1 units carry it, so under §9.4 it is stop-the-line. It is rated MAJOR as a gate hole that lets a finding class through. On this unit, the grammar point is not assessed at all by the item type that drills it.
findings.fix: Checker owner, with a test (CLAUDE.md: the rule belongs in the checker, never in a widened or narrowed accepted list). (1) In checkItem, an error_correction answer that equals its own quoted wrong sentence after the checker's normalisation is WRONG, never TYPO. (2) A single-token typed answer on a stem-vowel item is strict. Match the v2 topic (g.vokalwechsel, and the umlaut contrasts such as Konjunktiv II „hätte/hatte“) in checkOptionsFor, or grade any slip that turns the key into another form of the same verb as WRONG with tag Konjugation: the ihr-forms „schlaft“, „lest“, „trefft“ and the unchanged stem „sprechst“. Keep the foreign-keyboard allowance for ae/oe/ue respellings („schlaeft“ stays correct). SCHEMA owner: add a verb-form ErrorTag (u01 F15). Then tag ls2-p10, ls2-p01…p04, ls2-r01, ls2-r04 and c03, so that g.vokalwechsel gets a repair pool. Unit: no edit. Do not turn the typed items into choice items to route around the checker; that would also break the pool's recall mix (ITM-06).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-13 (or a new ITM rail) grades every item's known wrong forms with the player's own checkItem. (a) The quoted sentence of every error_correction must be WRONG. (b) For a typed gap whose key is a finite verb form with ä, ie or i (ü, ö) where the lemma's infinitive has a, e (o, u), the form without the vowel change must be WRONG. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u03-ls2-p10 (unchanged sentence → typo) and a1.1-u03-c03 („schlaft“ → typo); passing: ls1-p01 „mein“ → wrong. The test runs over all registered courses; today it fails in the nine units named above (a1.1-u03, -u07, -u08, -u10, -u12, a1.2-u04, a2.2-u04, b1.2-u04, b2.1-u04).
